relevance.rationale: Holographic-complexity paper: it supplies the calculations behind the conjecture that the quantum computational complexity of a holographic state equals the classical bulk action of a Wheeler-DeWitt patch, plus a review of information storage/processing bounds and the claim that black holes are the fastest computers. The folio has an information-theory chapter that does engage with horizons and computation (rem:p-vs-np-event-horizon, rem:information-paradox-incompleteness, rem:speed-of-light-regimes-lieb-robinson), so the subject overlaps. But the specific machinery has no counterpart here: there is no bulk/boundary duality, no action functional, and no complexity geometry in the corpus, and grep finds no 'complexity equals action' or 'Wheeler-DeWitt' anywhere in content/, nor any mention of this document's authors. The one piece that could dock — the processing-rate bounds recapped in its section 2 — is already covered by margolus1998 and lloyd2000, which rem:speed-of-light-regimes-lieb-robinson cites directly in its speed-limit comparison table. Adding this reference there would be decorative. Scope-(a): this document, as read, supplies nothing this folio can consume that it does not already cite.

proposedActions.rationale: Read and judged to need nothing; the block whose comparison table would have been the docking point already carries the two bound references it needs.
